Field Evaluation of the High Efficiency Dehumidification System (HEDS) at the Timken Museum of Art The National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) completed analysis of data collected at the Timken Museum of Art in San Diego, California as an assessment of the system performance of the Conservant Systems High Efficiency Dehumidification System (HEDS). Data was collected for measurement and verification (M&V) for several weeks during three evaluation periods: Summer (Aug-Sep 2023), Winter (Dec 2023-Feb 2024) and Spring (May-Jun 2024), while operating the Timken Museum’s HVAC system in several operating modes. This report provides details of the M&V measurements and analysis of data. Comparisons of the performance of the HEDS to different baseline configurations are provided to indicate the benefits that can be expected of the HEDS technology. 1 Description of the HEDS Figure 1 shows the configuration of the air handling unit (AHU) for the HEDS system. A primary feature of the HEDS is the use of a specially designed high efficiency cooling coil (CC in the schematic) and cooling recovery coil (CRC) that operate together to perform dehumidification and reheat of the supply air stream. HEDS reduces the cooling loads that must be served by the chiller plant and offers the potential to strongly reduce or eliminate the need for additional reheat energy while providing effective relative humidity (RH) control. For the conditions shown in Fig. 1, the air is cooled in the cooling coil from 71.06 °F (Air_inlet) to 53.68 °F (CC Drybulb) while the chilled water is heated from 48.8 °F (CHWS) to 64.5 °F (CRC_inlet) while passing through the CC.
